newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam City Cement sees high forex loss.
newsitem.headline: Siam City Cement sees high forex loss.

text.p: Siam City Cement Plc said on Friday it could face a 1.63 billion baht ($56.2 million) foreign exchange loss following the Thai baht's sharp depreciation since it switched to a managed float regime on July 2.

Siam City Cement said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand some $40.87 million of its foreign debt was due for repayment this year, which could leave the company with a 129.2 million baht foreign exchange loss if the baht stood at 29.00 to the dollar.
The baht fell to a new record low at about 29.900 on Friday morning, hit by jitters over the de facto devaluation of the Philippine peso and high dollar demand.

It said that expected foreign exchange losses would not erode its debt service position as it would partly be offset by over $100 million of annual foreign exchange earnings from its cement and construction materials exports.

The firm, the second biggest Thai cement producer, said it had found the cost of hedging against its foreign exchange exposure high currently and would start hedging activities only when costs eased to reasonable levels.
Thailand's biggest cement producer, Siam Cement Plc, also said on Thursday it may face foreign exchange losses of 9.9 billion baht if the baht weakened to 30.00 to the dollar.
